question: Can one fly brain hold language and chess at the same time?

shared_between_tasks.frozen: the 49,393-neuron / 9,050,172-edge graph and every synaptic weight
shared_between_tasks.trained: 148,179 per-neuron gain, rec_gain and bias -- the brain's dynamics
shared_between_tasks.note: The graph cannot be fought over because it does not move. The dynamics can, and both tasks must agree on one setting of them.

private_to_each_task.language: token embedding, in_proj, LayerNorm, rank-64 readout into 1,024 byte-BPE tokens
private_to_each_task.chess: 780 -> rank-64 -> 14,064 board encoder, LayerNorm, rank-64 trunk, 1,968 move head and 64-bin value head

matched_recipe.optimizer: AdamW, two-phase cosine, 1e-3 encoders / 1e-4 readouts then 3e-4 / 3e-5
matched_recipe.note: Identical in every respect to I32rank64fixed10k on the language side, so the language scores are directly comparable to Stage 6.

arms.note: The language forward pass still runs and still sets the schedule, so the chess side sees exactly the updates the joint arm sees; only its loss is switched off.

arms.role: both tasks, one brain, frozen synapses
both tasks, one brain, synapses allowed to adapt
arms.note: Every synapse gets a bounded sign-preserving multiplier, 1 + 0.1 tanh(theta), shared across the cell-type grouping. Tests whether giving the connectome itself capacity relieves a two-task squeeze.

reads_as.interference: M's language score against I, and M's chess score against C
reads_as.capacity: N against M; if sharing hurts and adapting the synapses recovers it, the squeeze was in the connectome rather than in the heads
